## TL;DR

I walked the Hub server picker headlessly (WebKit, Playwright, never a visible browser) at 375, 768 and 1280 px. The walk covered the empty, one-server, many-server, unreachable, add, edit, tailnet discovery and settings states, plus the add-form validation and duplicate errors. Nothing overflowed the viewport, every control had an accessible name, and the error copy was specific. The one real defect was keyboard focus on text fields: the picker removed the outline and relied on a 1px border colour shift. I added a 2px focus ring for those fields and pinned it with a test. The scoped check result is recorded in the handoff, not here.

## Work and rationale

The task names a "projects switcher" and a "server picker". In this repo the server picker is the native Hub app under `mobile/src` (server list, add/edit form, tailnet discovery). Tailnet discovery is where individual projects appear, each with a project name, so I treated it as the projects switcher. I did not walk the web TopBar repo pill in `src/ui-app`. That needs an authenticated `repoos serve`, which managed agents cannot run, so it is out of reach for this session.

To walk the app I ran the mobile Vite dev server from inside a scratch script, which the `?fixture=` query modes require. I installed `mobile/node_modules` from its lockfile first; the directory is gitignored. The scratch scripts live in `/tmp` and are not part of the change.

Walk results:

- Static render at all three widths: no element extended past the viewport (`scrollWidth` equal to the viewport width in every state). No `<button>`, link or input lacked an accessible name. Only the settings lock switch measured under 44px high (52×32), but its `switch-row` label is 44px tall, so the hit area meets the target size.
- Add form: empty submit shows "Enter a server URL."; `http://` shows the https hint; a 120-character host and a 120-character name stay inside the card; a duplicate URL names the existing server ("already saved as dev. Pick it from the list instead."). The error sits under the fields with `role="alert"`.
- Edit form: the URL is read-only and a hint explains why.
- Tailnet discovery: the loading line, saved, plain-http ("Needs HTTPS") and collapsed "Couldn't check these machines" groups all render and fit at 375.
- Screenshots at 375 and 1280 (list, add error, discovery) match the layout the existing `mobile-hub-*` tests describe.

The fix: `mobile/src/style.css` `.field input:focus` already set `outline: none` and changed `border-color` to `--ring`. Light and dark themes both produced a 1px border change, measured with computed styles, which is a faint cue. I added `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--ring)` so a focused field has a 2px ring. I confirmed in WebKit that the computed `box-shadow` is now set in both colour schemes. The class of the problem is every rule that drops an outline. `grep` finds only this one in `mobile/src`, so there was no sibling to patch.

The regression test goes in `src/ui-app/tests/mobile-hub-picker-layout.test.ts`, next to the existing layout assertions. It asserts that the focus rule keeps `outline: none` and a 1px `box-shadow` ring. That is a CSS-text check in the same style as the rest of that file, since jsdom cannot compute focus styles.

## Approaches tried

- First I used Tab from `body` to walk focus order. WebKit on macOS does not tab to buttons by default, so the walk stayed on `BODY` and told me nothing. I switched to explicit `focus()` and read `:focus-visible` and computed outline. Every button and the add-form input showed `outline: auto` (or the ring) at all three widths, so no fix was needed for buttons.
- I considered changing the picker's max-width at 768 and 1280. The mobile app is deliberately a centred phone-width column there, so I left it as is.
- I considered raising the settings toggle to 44px tall. The surrounding label already provides the 44px hit area, so I did not change the visual control.

## Challenges and blockers

- The mobile app had no installed dependencies in this worktree. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in `mobile/` fixed it with no lockfile change.
- The discovery walk without a fixture hits a real tailnet endpoint, so the console shows DNS and CORS errors. Those come from the sandbox having no network, not from the app, and the `?fixture=discover` path avoids them.
- Visual confirmation is limited to the captures in this session. The Hub app is not a web route on the RepoOS server, so no `## Shots` entry can target it. A human should look at the focus ring on a device if they want more than the computed-style check.

## Key learnings

- On WebKit, Tab-order checks need explicit focus. Otherwise a missing focus ring and a headless quirk look the same.
- A fixture-driven Vite dev server is a good walk target: it exercises states a real server cannot produce on demand, such as unreachable hosts and discovery results, without any credentials.
- Measure focus with computed style, not by eye: a 1px border colour shift looked adequate in a screenshot but was only a 1px cue in the numbers.
